conviction_note: BlueNord has been a fixed-ratio merger target of Vår Energi since 21 July 2026 (9.7153 VAR shares + NOK 76.83 cash per share, plus compensation for any VAR dividend before closing), so its window move is about 0.8x whatever Vår Energi does on 28 October plus a small spread term; its own Q3 production is already out and inside guidance, and it is not paying a dividend before closing. That leaves only the spread: a 2.4% discount that has widened from about 0.5-1% in late September, which could tighten if the release reports approvals. That gives +0.3 on the findings and almost exactly 50/50 on the sign.

findings.finding: BNOR is pinned to Vår Energi by a fixed exchange ratio (9.7153 VAR + NOK 76.83 cash per share). Since the deal, BNOR's daily returns have run at corr 0.94 and beta 0.80 to VAR (69 sessions to 2026-10-27), and the median absolute residual is 0.35% a day, so BlueNord's own Q3 numbers have almost no route to the price.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Before the deal BNOR's results days moved -4.3% to +8.7% (Q2 2026 +6.96%). No results day has fallen inside the merger period yet. Vår Energi's own Q3 day (2026-10-21) moved BNOR +0.65% against VAR +1.1%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is not mispriced; it is the scale of the move. A 2% history median taken from pre-deal results days overstates how far BNOR can travel on its own news. If the market were treating BNOR as a standalone producer, its returns would not track VAR at 0.94 correlation, and they do.
findings.independence: Daily closes BNOR.OL and VAR.OL from Yahoo chart API https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/BNOR.OL?range=6mo&interval=1d

findings.finding: The merger spread is about 2.4% (BNOR 632 against about NOK 647 of consideration, intraday 2026-10-27) with completion guided 'around year-end'. That is wider than the 0.2-1.2% it held from 8 Sep to 6 Oct. It opened up as VAR rallied about 15% in October and BNOR lagged (e.g. 2026-10-23: VAR +3.5%, BNOR +2.1%). A release confirming conditions met, or a firm closing date, would close part of that gap within the session.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance. The spread narrowed from about 4-5% to about 1% around the 24 Aug EGM approval, the only step in the conditions so far.
findings.why_not_priced: The spread itself is priced risk. What may not be priced is that BlueNord's own release is the first BlueNord document since VAR's 21 Oct report, and it may update the status of the Danish approvals. If the market expected that status to firm up, the spread would not have widened from about 1% to 2.4% over October. It is equally possible that the widening reflects a timing risk the market sees and I cannot, which is why the size is small and p_up stays near 50.
findings.independence: Merger plan conditions precedent (Danish Ministry, Danish Business Authority, EU, partner consents; long-stop 1 June 2027): https://www.bluenord.com/content/uploads/2026/07/BlueNord-and-Var-Energi-Merger-Plan.pdf

outside_window.finding: Vår Energi EGM on 11 Nov 2026 to approve the Q3 dividend of NOK 1.368/share (record 18 Nov). BNOR holders get this value either as VAR holders or as cash compensation, so it is neutral to the spread.
Completion of the merger 'around year-end', after which BNOR delists into VAR. The remaining spread of about 2.4% accrues at completion.

baseline_tension: The baseline lean of -0.5 comes from the run-up alone (+10.1% in 20 days), and that run-up is simply VAR's October rally passed through the fixed ratio. A short register reading zero tells us nothing in an arbitrage situation. The spread finding leans mildly positive, against the run-up lean, and the gap is small.

lessons_applied: 'In a live bid, results are noise; the offer is the finding' confirmed the framing already in the draft. Findings unchanged.

'Too small about the move': abs_move_pct raised from 1.3 to 1.4. It stays well under the 3% pre-released base because a fixed-ratio target travels at about 0.8x Vår Energi's daily volatility (BNOR daily sd 1.37% since the deal). This is a structural cap, not a reaction-history cap.
